fi-diademichthys-lineatus.title: Yellow Stripe Clingfish (Urchin Clingfish)
fi-diademichthys-lineatus.summary: A tiny, striped clingfish that lives among long-spined Diadema urchins and branching corals in the Indo-Pacific. It picks small prey from tight spaces with its long snout.
rows: About 2 in (Top Shelf adult size); wild record 5 cm (2 in) TL (FishBase)
Carnivore. Foods: live copepods, enriched brine shrimp, mysis shrimp, crustacean eggs, frozen carnivore preparations, finely chopped marine fish, chopped squid
Western Indian Ocean: Oman and Mauritius
notes: Mature live rock and a refugium help, since it relies on copepods and other tiny prey; keep only with small, calm fish.
warn: Can release toxic mucus from its skin when handled or stressed: move it in a container, not a net (Top Shelf).

fi-platax-orbicularis.title: Orbic Batfish
fi-platax-orbicularis.summary: A disc-shaped batfish that changes from a silvery, barred juvenile into a tan-brown adult with tall fins. Peaceful but it grows very large and needs a big, deep tank.
rows: About 20–22 in (Saltwaterfish.com adult size); wild record 60 cm (23.6 in) TL (FishBase)
Carnivore: start new fish on live saltwater feeder shrimp, then frozen meaty foods such as shrimp, krill, squid and scallop plus herbivore mixes, two or three times a day
Indo-Pacific: Red Sea and East Africa and Persian Gulf to the Tuamoto Islands, north to southern Japan, south to northern Australia and New Caledonia
notes: Batfish are prone to ich; quarantine carefully.
warn: Not for reef tanks: it eats corals, anemones and other sessile invertebrates, plus small fish.
